connector.instructions:
oasis-code is a harness on the user's computer: its agents read, search and change files, run commands and research there.

current_session names the session whose director turn waits on this chat, if any. Projects are opened folders (list_projects, open_project). A session is one task: a working folder, its main agent's conversation, and every participant, separate task, relay and interaction started in it (create_session makes one).

An agent receives only what its run is given: the call's text (or the stored original message named by source_turn_id), the attachments and mentions passed, answers handed over by receive_run_ids or a step's receives, its own conversation and its workspace's files. Nothing of this chat reaches an agent otherwise.

Calls that start work return at once; a run continues after the call (about a minute is the limit of one call). get_run reads an ended run's whole final answer in pages, waiting up to wait_s for an active one. get_collaboration reads a session's participants, conversations, groups and the edges between runs. read_file and bash work in a session's folder directly.

The same request_id with the same request returns what the first call started; with a different request it is refused. Permissions, approvals, checks and protected paths belong to the user.

tools.name: current_session
tools.description: The oasis-code session whose director turn waits on this chat, if any, and whether oasis-code reads this chat.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List model routes, IDs, availability, context windows, input capabilities and supported thinking efforts (null when unknown).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List opened folders (projects) and their sessions.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Open a folder as a project. mode sets how agents reach the folder. With reuse (default true), a folder already open returns its existing project.

path.description: An absolute folder path on the user's machine.

name.description: The project's name. Default: the folder's name.

instructions.description: Standing instructions every run of the project reads first.

reuse.description: Return the existing project of this folder when there is one. Default: true.

mode.description: direct: agents edit the folder itself (each run's file edits can be undone in the app); snapshot: agents work on a copy; attached: agents read the original with the user's current access permissions.

request_id.description: Key for this request, 8 to 100 characters. The same key with the same request returns what the first call started; the same key with a different request is refused.

tools.name: set_project_config
tools.description: Add to a project's instructions, checks or protected paths, or set its default model. Omitted fields stay unchanged; the checks and protected paths the project has cannot be removed or changed here.

instructions.description: Standing instructions every run of the project reads first.

checks.description: [{id, command, parser: pytest|node_test|exit_code, timeout_s, required}]; the project's checks stay as they are.

protected_paths.description: Globs no run may write; the project's protected paths stay protected.

default_model.description: The model new sessions of the project use.

tools.name: create_session
tools.description: Create a session in a project: a working folder of its own and a main agent's conversation; the participants, runs and groups started in it belong to it. A native director creates sessions only in its own session's project; a session it creates is reachable by its later calls.

project_id.description: The project. Native director: omitted means this director's project, the only one it may name.

title.description: The session's title, shown in oasis-code. Default: New task.

model.description: Model ID from list_models. Omitted: the session's model.

request_id.description: Key for this request, 8 to 100 characters. The same key with the same request returns what the first call started; the same key with a different request is refused.

tools.name: get_session
tools.description: Read a session: its runs with participant, origin and placement, pending approvals, and a summary of its collaboration (participants, and counts of groups, edges and thread items).

session_id.description: Session ID. Omitted: the session whose director turn waits on this chat, when exactly one does.

tools.name: get_collaboration
tools.description: Read the collaboration record of a session, of one run, or of one participant: participants, their conversations, groups (interactions and relays), runs, thread items, and the typed edges between runs (continues, forks, after, received, cited, workspace, dispatched, note). A received edge means an answer was handed over whole; a cited edge means a run was named without its content. Lists are paged with cursor.

session_id.description: Session to read. Omitted with run_id and participant_id also omitted: as session_id elsewhere.

run_id.description: Instead of a session: one run, with its participant, conversation and the edges into and out of it.

participant_id.description: Instead of a session: one participant (pa_…), with its runs newest first.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page. Omitted: the first page.

limit.description: Items per list on a page, 1 to 100. Default: 50.

tools.name: post_director_note
tools.description: Record one exchange of this chat in a session's thread, for a session that does not read this chat.

model.description: The model that answered, as the chat shows it.

source.description: Where the conversation is held. Default: chatgpt.

tools.name: start_run
tools.description: Start a run of an agent; the call returns at once with the run it started (or the interaction step it queued, see resume_run_id) and the run continues after it. By default the message goes to the session's main agent and continues its conversation. resume_run_id continues the participant of that ended run; separate starts a separate task. source_turn_id uses the stored original message of that user turn. cites and receive_run_ids name ended runs of the same session.

session_id.description: Session ID. Omitted: the session whose director turn waits on this chat, when exactly one does.

text.description: Message for the agent. Required unless source_turn_id is given.

source_turn_id.description: A user turn of this session with a stored original message: its text, attachments, mentions, thinking, budget and the run it continues are used for this call; text, attachments and mentions are then not given. Omitted: no stored message is used.

request_id.description: Key for this request, 8 to 100 characters. The same key with the same request returns what the first call started; the same key with a different request is refused.

model.description: Model ID from list_models. Omitted: the session's model.

thinking.description: Thinking effort: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Omitted: the model's default.

attachments.description: Session attachment asset IDs (images, UTF-8 text/code, PDF, video) uploaded through the session API. Route capabilities apply; PDF and video support is route-specific. A separate task takes no attachments.

fresh.description: Start the main agent's conversation without its earlier history. Default: false.

mentions.description: File or symbol references passed with the message.

separate.description: Start a separate task: a new participant, a new conversation and a workspace of its own (a copy of the session files; over a direct or attached folder, an output folder of its own with the folder read-only). It is shown on a card of its own and summarised in the thread. Cannot be combined with resume_run_id. Default: false.

resume_run_id.description: Ended run to continue: the new run belongs to the same participant and continues its conversation and files; a participant of an interaction continues as a step of that interaction, counted in its budget. While that interaction runs and cannot start the step yet, the call returns the queued step instead of a run (status queued, interaction_id, node_id, participant_id; run_id null): its run starts when the interaction's queue reaches it, and its end is reported as a run's end is. Cannot be combined with separate.

expected_head_run_id.description: With resume_run_id: the latest run of that participant's conversation as last read; the call is refused if the conversation moved on since.

base_checkpoint_id.description: Saved file version a separate task starts from. Omitted: the session's current files.

constraints.description: Restrictions of a separate task or of a follow-up: they narrow, never widen, the user's permissions.

cites.description: Ended runs of the same session this call refers to, each by run_id with an optional note; at most 8. Recorded as cited edges; the agent is told the run and participant of each, not their content.

receive_run_ids.description: Ended runs of the same session whose final answers are added whole to the new run's opening message, each with its tool-call lines and measured facts; at most 6. Recorded as received edges; they add to the run's input.

tools.name: start_relay
tools.description: Start a relay in a session: 2 to 6 agents take turns on one message in the order given, each turn in the session's working folder and reading the earlier turns, for the given number of rounds. Returns the first turn's run; the harness starts each later turn when the one before it ends. cites and receive_run_ids go with the first turn's opening message only; each later turn is handed the earlier turns' answers by the relay itself.

session_id.description: Session ID. Omitted: the session whose director turn waits on this chat, when exactly one does.

text.description: The message every turn is given. Required unless source_turn_id is given.

source_turn_id.description: A user turn of this session with a stored original message: its text, attachments, mentions, thinking, budget and the run it continues are used for this call; text, attachments and mentions are then not given. Omitted: no stored message is used.

agents.description: The agents in turn order, 2 to 6, each by model ID; one model may be listed more than once.

rounds.description: Rounds, 1 to 5: every agent takes one turn per round. Default: 1.

thinking.description: Thinking effort: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Omitted: the model's default.

attachments.description: Session attachment asset IDs (images, UTF-8 text/code, PDF, video) uploaded through the session API. Route capabilities apply; PDF and video support is route-specific. A separate task takes no attachments.

mentions.description: File or symbol references passed with the message.

fresh.description: Start the first turn without the thread's earlier history. Default: false.

resume_run_id.description: Ended run of the session's thread whose conversation the first turn continues.

request_id.description: Key for this request, 8 to 100 characters. The same key with the same request returns what the first call started; the same key with a different request is refused.

cites.description: Ended runs of the same session this call refers to, each by run_id with an optional note; at most 8. Recorded as cited edges; the agent is told the run and participant of each, not their content.

tools.name: attach_image
tools.description: Attach a PNG, JPEG or WebP to a session: up to 5 MiB and 8000 pixels per side. Returns its asset_id, for start_run's attachments.

session_id.description: Session ID. Omitted: the session whose director turn waits on this chat, when exactly one does.

name.description: A label for the image, shown in the thread. Default: image.

data_base64.description: The image's bytes, base64 (a data: URL prefix is accepted).

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Read a run: for an ended run, its final answer (receipt.final_text of that exact run) 6000 characters per page, its receipt and its edges; or its recorded steps (view events). An active run returns its status; wait_s waits up to 55 seconds for it to end.

view.description: result or events. result: the final answer 6000 characters per page (final_text_chars is its length, next_cursor reads on), the receipt and the run's edges. events: the recorded steps, 40 per page. Default: result.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous page of the same view. Omitted: the first page.

wait_s.description: Seconds to wait for an active run to end, 0 to 55. Default: 0.

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.description: Stop a run. File changes it completed remain.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Read a working folder, its source_mount read-only boundary and saved file versions. include_diff includes file changes.

path.description: Relative file path the diff is limited to.

cursor.description: Cursor returned with a truncated diff.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file with line numbers, or list a folder. next_offset continues.

path.description: File or folder path relative to the working folder. Default: the folder itself.

offset.description: First line or folder entry, starting at 1. Default: 1.

limit.description: Most lines or folder entries, 1 to 2000. Default: 400; a folder page holds at most 500.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run a shell command in a session's working folder, sandboxed as an agent's command is, under the session's permissions. Returns the exit code and the head and tail of its output; a command still running returns its execution_id to wait on again. An attached folder is a symlink there (grep -r needs its name with a trailing slash).

command.description: The command, run by the shell.

execution_id.description: Instead of a command: one still running, to wait on and read again.

cwd.description: Folder to run in, relative to the working folder.

wait_s.description: Seconds to wait before returning, 0 to 55. Default: 30.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before the command is stopped. Default: the harness's.

tools.name: start_interaction
tools.description: Create an interaction in a session: 2 to 6 participants, each with its own conversation and an isolated output workspace (a direct or attached source folder is mounted read-only). Its plan is one of: mode independent (each participant answers once, without the others' answers); mode discussion (then cross_rounds waves, each handed the other participants' complete previous answers); mode director (the session's director is asked for the plan in a turn of its own); nodes (the steps given, run in their dependency order). Every run counts against max_runs (at most 30). Returns the interaction, its participants, nodes, workspaces and started runs.

session_id.description: Session ID. Omitted: the session whose director turn waits on this chat, when exactly one does.

text.description: The message every participant's first step is given. Required unless source_turn_id is given.

source_turn_id.description: A user turn of this session with a stored original message: its text, attachments, mentions, thinking, budget and the run it continues are used for this call; text, attachments and mentions are then not given. Omitted: no stored message is used.

participants.description: 2 to 6 participants, each by model ID with an optional thinking effort and an optional id (letters, digits, - or _) that nodes name it by; one model may be listed more than once.

mode.description: independent, discussion or director. Omitted with nodes omitted: independent. Cannot be combined with nodes.

cross_rounds.description: discussion: waves after the first answers, 1 to 4. Default: 1.

nodes.description: Instead of mode: the steps, in the format schedule takes; the harness runs them in their dependency order.

then.description: With nodes: after the last step, stop or director. Default: stop.

thinking.description: Thinking effort: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Omitted: the model's default.

attachments.description: Session attachment asset IDs (images, UTF-8 text/code, PDF, video) uploaded through the session API. Route capabilities apply; PDF and video support is route-specific. A separate task takes no attachments.

mentions.description: File or symbol references passed with the message.

max_runs.description: Most runs the interaction may start, 1 to 30.

request_id.description: Key for this request, 8 to 100 characters. The same key with the same request returns what the first call started; the same key with a different request is refused.

cites.description: Ended runs of the same session this call refers to, each by run_id with an optional note; at most 8. Recorded as cited edges; the agent is told the run and participant of each, not their content.

tools.name: schedule
tools.description: Add steps to an interaction's plan. Each step is one run of one participant: it starts once the steps it depends on have ended, is handed the whole answers of the steps it receives and of the runs in its receive_runs, and works on the workspace given. A plan with a problem is refused whole, with every problem named.

title.description: A few words for the session's title, used while the session has no title of the user's.

nodes.description: The steps. id: a short name (letters, digits, - or _). participant: the participant's id as the interaction lists it. depends_on: steps that end first; a step also comes after everything those wait for. receives: steps among those it comes after whose answers it is handed whole; a participant's own earlier answers are in its conversation already. workspace: own (the participant's own copy, kept for all its steps), shared (the session's working folder, one step at a time) or another step's id (that step's copy, after it); in a session that edits its folder in place every step works in that folder. instruction: text added to the step's message. cites: ended runs of the session named to the step without their content. receive_runs: ended runs of the session whose answers the step is handed whole.

then.description: After the last step: stop (the interaction ends and the user decides) or director (the director is asked what comes next). Default: stop.

expected_revision.description: The plan revision as last read; the call is refused if the plan changed since. Omitted on a first plan.

tools.name: integrate
tools.description: Apply saved file versions (checkpoints) of runs to a working folder. Conflicts or a changed destination stop the operation. Configured checks run before the changes are applied.

checkpoint_ids.description: Saved file version IDs to apply, in order.

note.description: A note recorded with the integration.

native.instructions:
This conversation is a director session of oasis-code, a harness on the user's computer. Each turn begins with a context line naming the session, its project and its working folder. A turn carries one of: a message the user wrote to this director, with its original envelope (its turn id, mentions, attachment metadata and thinking choices); an app note that runs or groups started from this conversation ended; an app note about an interaction's plan.

Agents work in sessions. An agent receives only what its run is given: the call's text (or the stored original message named by source_turn_id), the attachments and mentions passed, answers handed over by receive_run_ids or a step's receives, its own conversation and its workspace's files. Nothing else of this conversation reaches an agent. A user may name an agent as @[Label](agent:<route>); the route is a model ID.

Calls that start work return at once with what they started; runs continue after the call. When a run or a group started from this conversation ends, the harness adds an app note to this conversation as a new turn; a turn does not wait for runs. get_run reads an ended run's whole final answer in pages of 6000 characters; get_session and get_collaboration read participants, conversations, groups and the edges between runs.

Calls reach this director's session and the sessions its own create_session calls created (in the same project); a call that names anything else is refused. While a turn answers the end of an isolated interaction, calls that start or change work are refused. cancel_run needs the director session's allow_destructive setting.

Every run uses the user's model quota; a higher thinking effort takes longer and uses more. Permissions, approvals, checks and protected paths belong to the user; a call they do not allow is refused with its reason.

tools.description: Add steps to an interaction's plan. Each step is one run of one participant: it starts once the steps it depends on have ended, is handed the whole answers of the steps it receives and of the runs in its receive_runs, and works on the workspace given. A plan with a problem is refused whole, with every problem named.

title.description: A few words for the session's title, used while the session has no title of the user's.

nodes.description: The steps. id: a short name (letters, digits, - or _). participant: the participant's id as the interaction lists it. depends_on: steps that end first; a step also comes after everything those wait for. receives: steps among those it comes after whose answers it is handed whole; a participant's own earlier answers are in its conversation already. workspace: own (the participant's own copy, kept for all its steps), shared (the session's working folder, one step at a time) or another step's id (that step's copy, after it); in a session that edits its folder in place every step works in that folder. instruction: text added to the step's message. cites: ended runs of the session named to the step without their content. receive_runs: ended runs of the session whose answers the step is handed whole.

then.description: After the last step: stop (the interaction ends and the user decides) or director (the director is asked what comes next). Default: stop.

expected_revision.description: The plan revision as last read; the call is refused if the plan changed since. Omitted on a first plan.

tools.name: integrate
tools.description: Apply saved file versions (checkpoints) of runs to a working folder. Conflicts or a changed destination stop the operation. Configured checks run before the changes are applied.

checkpoint_ids.description: Saved file version IDs to apply, in order.

note.description: A note recorded with the integration.

templates.director.envelope: Original message envelope of user turn {turn_id} (a call with source_turn_id {turn_id} uses it; attachment IDs are forwarded unchanged): {envelope}
templates.director.task_event:
App note: Runs ended: {run_ids}.
This note is from the harness, not from the user. get_run reads each final answer whole, 6000 characters per page.
templates.director.person_runs:
App note: Since the last turn, these runs ended that were not started from this conversation: {run_ids}.
get_run reads each one.
templates.director.plan_title: Session title: none yet. schedule's title names the session.
templates.director.plan_in_place: Folder: this session edits its folder in place, so there are no copies here: every step works in that one folder, whatever its workspace says, and the steps that write take turns.
templates.director.plan_images: {count}, seen by every participant's first step (not by you)
templates.director.decide:
App note: Interaction {interaction_id}: every step of the plan ended.
Steps:
{steps}
Runs left in the budget: {runs_left}.
schedule adds steps (depends_on may name ended steps; receives hands their answers on whole; a participant keeps its workspace). An answer of this turn without a schedule call ends the interaction, and the user decides what to adopt.
templates.director.plan_none: the director planned nothing; continue asks it again
templates.director.native_wait_refusal: wait_s is not available to this director: a turn does not wait for runs. When a run started from this conversation ends, the harness adds an app note to the conversation. Nothing was waited for.
templates.director.session_refusal: This call names something outside the sessions this director reaches ({session_ids}), or things of more than one session. Nothing was run.
templates.director.report_only_refusal: This turn answers the end of an isolated interaction: calls that start or change work are refused in it. Nothing was run.
templates.director.destructive_refusal: {tool} is not allowed in this director session: its config does not allow destructive calls. Nothing was changed.
templates.director.project_refusal: A session can be created only in this director's project ({project_id}). Nothing was created.
